original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Certified bit-side budgets for priority revision 3: in the coverage-law relaxation of the selected PR589 bit word (fixed local word or most favorable in-window shapes, idle mass at the halving-guard cap 45, fractional counts, no surcharge), the packing ceiling, each revision-3 lever and combination at a = 1/99, and the joint copy-charge x helper-count x helper-width surface, with scoped obstructions O1 (copy charge 63) and O2 (centre path shared by two calls against the design-free helper floors).
scope_change_reason: The card's helper-interface question is saturated or claimed (semantic-D contract #1194/#1311, entrances #1179/#1253, after-B frames #1128; register-model card actively claimed in #1317), while revision 3 (#1272) quantifies its levers on the complex side only and #1293 leaves the bit word's realizability-aware ceiling open. The bit-side budget answers what any bit helper or centre-path mechanism must meet to reach the 1/99 planning target.
bottleneck_link: A large kappa jump needs both suppliers to advance (bottleneck brief, priority log). This gives the bit side's quantitative targets: which levers can reach 1/99 under the coverage law, and how many helpers of which width a given copy charge leaves room for. It also shows that the combined lever of #1272 (and its bit analogue) relies on rank-16 children beyond the stage window. No kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop once every lever, surface boundary and obstruction is certified with exact intervals and the positive controls reproduce the selected bit endpoint and #1240's complex ceiling; report any undecided boundary instead of claiming it.
evidence: RESULT.json: bit word packing ceiling 0.001955918756 (cap 45); centre free x2.771, shared x1.885, two unpaid x3.738, rank-8 x1.642, rank-16 x2.419; centre free + rank-8 0.00894 < 1/99; centre free + rank-16 0.01317 and centre free + two unpaid 0.01076 pass. O1: copy charge 63 fails 1/99 at caps 42/45/63 even helper-free (ceiling 0.00679 at cap 45). O2: with the centre path shared (copy charge 31.5) at cap 45, at most 104 width-8 helpers fit (k=104 passes, 105 fails), below both floors (138 strict, 212 sink-only); only width <= 4 meets the strict floor and width 2 the sink-only floor. Complex cross-check: #1240's ceiling reproduced; #1272's combined lever gives 0.01101 with rank-16 children but 0.00813 < 1/99 inside the window (rank 9). 12 tests pass.
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
